elements.evidence: "grants to Customer, its affiliates and its contractors acting on Customer's behalf"

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
Paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable
elements.evidence: Licence is "royalty-free"; no paid-up licence exists in this grant, so the condition is demonstrably absent

elements.element: Subscription licences terminable/revocable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: "revocable only upon expiration or termination of this Agreement in accordance with paragraph 4" — tied to any termination, not to uncured material breach
"transferable to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction or to a purchaser of all or substantially all of Customer's assets"
Affiliates are covered outright in the grant: "to Customer, its affiliates" (exceeds notice-conditioned coverage)

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: "transferable to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction"

offending_extra_words: transferable to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction or to a purchaser of all or substantially all of Customer's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement,
reasons: Preferred level is incomplete: revocation is tied to "expiration or termination of this Agreement" generally rather than to termination for uncured material breach, so the subscription-licence element fails.
Fallback is fully met (affiliates covered without any notice condition; transfer to an M&A successor expressly permitted), so the clause sits at the fallback.

Minimality fails: the edit rewrites the grant, expanding 19 words to 70 (ratio 3.68) and changing 73.5% of characters, exceeding the official gates; an operator/short-phrase edit (e.g. deleting "revocable" and adding ", its affiliates and its contractors acting on Customer's behalf") would suffice.
The deletion of "without right of sublicense" and "non-assignable" grants new sublicensing/assignment rights not required by the preferred position — sublicensing is a distinct concept.
The transferability language duplicates the successor-assignment permission already present in clause (h), creating redundant protection.
